beats.care: If someone pays you to use your bank account or SIM, refuse. Account owners land in trouble too. A 19-year-old was arrested here.
beats.what: Hyderabad cybercrime police arrested two men who got about 70 students, delivery workers and others to hand over bank accounts and SIM cards.
beats.why: The accounts were sent to Haryana and used in over 450 frauds across India, police said.

cards.body: DCP S. Chaitanya Kumar said a 39-year-old ex-cab driver and an accomplice collected passbooks, debit cards, net-banking logins and SIMs for a commission, and couriered them to Haryana. A 19-year-old opened three accounts for him. A third man is absconding.
A bank account in an ordinary person's name that scammers use to receive and move stolen money. It hides the real crooks, so police reach the account owner first.
cards.title: what's a mule account?

cards.body: The case started with a Facebook scam promising ₹45 lakh for an old one-rupee note. The victim lost about ₹7.9 lakh instead.
Police say about 70 accounts were used in these cases across India.
cards.caption: Fraud cases linked to these accounts

cards.q: A friend says they 'rent out' their bank account for cash. What do you do?

opts: To move stolen money without it tracing back to them
cards.q: Why do scammers want other people's bank accounts?
cards.why: Mule accounts hide the real scammers, which is why the account owner ends up facing police.
